o.text:
From Proto-Turkic *yor- (“to interpret”). Cognate with Turkish yormak (“interpret”), Turkmen ýormak (“to foretell, interpret”), Kyrgyz жоруу (joruu, “to interpret”), Kazakh жору (joruw, “to interpret”).
The development of the coda-final /z/ remains unclear. Possibilities include an expected development of the Proto-Turkic /*ŕ/, which was unexpectedly turned into /r/ instead of /z/ in all other cognates (as in reflexes of *köŕ- (“to see”)); or development of the variant *yod-, as reflected in dialectal Turkish yoymak, Uzbek yoʻymoq and joʻymoq.

From qüvvət (“strength”) + -li.
Cognate with Bashkir ҡеүәтле (qiwätli), Kazakh қуатты (quwattı), Tatar куәтле (quwätle), Turkish kuvvetli, Turkmen kuwwatly, Uyghur قۇۋۋەتلى (quwwetli), Uzbek quvvatli.

Likely from Late Ottoman Turkish درنك (dernek), a learned borrowing from a medieval Turkic language, such as Karakhanid تِرْناكْ (tẹrnek, “people's gathering, a public assembly”), from earlier *tẹringek, from *tērin-, a passive/reflexive form of Proto-Common Turkic *tēr- (“to gather, collect”). Compare Azerbaijani dərmək.
Borrowed from Classical Persian آسمانی (āsmānī). By surface analysis, asman + -i.
Borrowed from Arabic حَوَارِيّ (ḥawāriyy), from Ge'ez ሐዋርያ (ḥäwarəya, “traveller; messenger, envoy; apostle”).
